War of Genesis: Idle Loot class tier list for PvE and PvP
War of Genesis: Idle Loot class tier list for PvE and PvP
By
Mohammad Sadiq
Modified Sep 17, 2026 10:44 GMT 
Discuss
The best classes in the game (Image via New Normal Soft Inc.)

War of Genesis: Idle Loot has multiple classes on offer, each with its distinct playstyle and abilities. While we’d be tempted to say that they’re all great in their own right, some are greater than others, necessitating the need for this tier list.

Ad

In this tier list, we shall split the War of Genesis: Idle Loot class across three different tiers. Which tier a class falls in depends on its viability across PvE and PvP, so the higher the tier, the better the results you can expect.

The three classes in War of Genesis: Idle Loot have been split across three tiers below. As stated earlier, we’ve done so based on their overall competency and viability in PvE and PvP. S-Tier represents the strongest class in the game, A represents the class that falls just a little short, and B is the weakest.

S-Tier class in War of Genesis: Idle Loot

The Wizard class falls under S-Tier. This class comes with the highest base damage in the game, allowing you to mow down most enemies with ease. The damage only increases further as you unlock characters when levelling up, so no enemy is ever a hurdle.

Its base defense and HP are just a little short of the Knight, but not short enough to make a difference. You’ll get a similar level of tankiness and survivability to the Knight, while having a massive damage output, making the Wizard the best class to pick in the game in both PvE and PvP.

Ad
A-Tier class in War of Genesis: Idle Loot

The Knight class falls under A-Tier in the game. The Knight has the highest base HP and defense. As stated earlier, while these stats are the highest for the Knight, the Wizard trails incredibly close, making the two interchangeable. The only real difference comes down to damage, where the Wizard takes the lead.

Still, the Knight is incredible in his own right. The class comes with a stun ability that allows you to create breathing room in combat encounters. The class also has immense AOE damage potential, making it a strong pick for any fight, be it PvE or PvP.

Ad
B-Tier class in War of Genesis: Idle Loot

The final class, the Ranger, falls under the B-Tier in the game. This class excels in movement speed and attack speed, but falls short in everything else. If you’re a beginner, however, we recommend sticking to the Ranger. The class excels at farming loot due to its pace, making it strong in PvE.

In PvP, however, the lack of damage output sticks out like a sore thumb, putting you at a disadvantage against others. If you’re in solely for the grind, consider using the Ranger, or else you’re better off using the others.
